verses.1: When Rama had thus spoken about that wonderful birth of Pururavas, Lakshmana and the highly renowned Bharata spoke again.
verses.2: O best of men, you ought to tell us the truth about what Ila did after she resided with Budha, the son of Soma, for a year.
verses.3: Having heard the sweet words of those two who were questioning, Rama again told this story, O daughter of Prajapati.
verses.4: When the brave one (Ila/Sudyumna) attained manhood, the highly renowned and extremely intelligent Budha invited the exceedingly generous sage Samvarta.
verses.5: He also invited Chyavana, the son of Bhrigu, the sage Arishtanemi, Pramodana who brings joy, and then the sage Durvasas.
verses.6: Having gathered all these, the eloquent and perceptive Budha spoke to all his well-composed friends with patience.
verses.7: He said, "This mighty-armed king, Ila, is the son of Kardama; know him as he truly is, and indeed, let his welfare be ensured in this matter."
verses.8: Just as they were conversing, the greatly refulgent Kardama approached that hermitage along with other great-souled brahmins.
verses.9: Pulastya, Kratu, Vaṣaṭkāra, and the greatly effulgent Oṅkāra also similarly approached that hermitage.
verses.10: All of them, delighted at their mutual meeting and being well-wishers of the king of Bālhika, then spoke different words.
verses.11: Kardama then spoke words that were supremely beneficial for the sake of a son, saying, "O brahmins, listen to my words which are indeed for the welfare of the king."
verses.12: I see no other remedy except Lord Shiva, and there is no sacrifice superior to the Ashvamedha, which is indeed dear to the great-souled one; therefore, let us all perform the formidable Ashvamedha sacrifice for the sake of the king.
verses.13: All the eminent Brahmins, thus addressed by Kardama, approved of that sacrifice intended for the worship of Rudra.
verses.14: The renowned Marutta, a disciple of the royal sage Samvarta and a conqueror of cities, then performed that sacrifice.
verses.15: A great sacrifice then took place near Budha's hermitage, and the highly renowned Rudra attained supreme satisfaction.
verses.16: Then, when the sacrifice was concluded, the lord of Uma, pleased and filled with supreme joy, addressed all the brahmins there in Ila's presence.
verses.17: Rudra declared, "O best among Brahmins, I am pleased by this horse sacrifice and by your devotion; what pleasing and auspicious thing shall I do for this lord of Bahlika?"
verses.18: When the lord of gods spoke thus, those attentive Brahmins propitiated him so that Ila might indeed become a man again.
verses.19: Then, the greatly effulgent Mahadeva, being pleased, restored Ila to manhood, and having done so, he disappeared.
verses.20: After the horse sacrifice was concluded, Hara disappeared, and all the wise Brahmins returned to their respective places as they had come.
verses.21: But the king, having left Bahli, established the glorious and unsurpassed city of Pratishthana in the central region.
verses.22: The royal sage Shashabindu, a conqueror of cities, ruled Bahli, while the powerful King Ila, son of Prajapati, ruled in Pratishthana.
verses.23: In due course, King Ila attained the unsurpassed divine realm of Brahma, and his son, King Pururava Aila, then obtained Pratishthana.
verses.24: Indeed, such is the power of the Ashwamedha sacrifice, O best among men, that one who had become a woman regained manhood and obtained other things that are difficult to achieve. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे नवतितमः सर्गः ।। 90 ।। Thus ends the ninetieth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
